You can get around the city and can have basic conversations with the locals, but are unsure of all of the complexities of social life in this country. You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "That was a really good thing that she did. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks you, saying his home is not far away. You take several of the bags from him and see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, you both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks you and says you have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Was that you who helped that man?" You say it was. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks you, saying his home is not far away. You take several of the bags from him and see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, you both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks you and says you have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Was that you who helped that man?" You say it was. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on the outside. "Nice day we're having, right?" You say it is. The barista continues, "Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

Imagine that you are in a foreign country and have only a basic understanding of the local customs and practices. You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"

You aren't quite sure which actions are expected and required of people.     A couple of days into your trip, you are walking to a nearby coffeehouse. As you are crossing a street, up ahead you notice an older man visibly struggling to walk, carrying several bags of heavy groceries. You see a woman run over to the man and ask if he would like help with carrying everything. He accepts and thanks her, saying his home is not far away. She takes several of the bags from him and you see him walk a bit easier now. Once across the street, they both walk another block before the older man stops in front of a building, thanks her and says they have arrived. He collects his groceries and goes inside. You see the woman keep walking. You walk farther down the block and enter the coffeehouse. As you do so, you see the barista standing at the window, watching the street. It looks like she saw what happened.     Once in the coffeehouse, you order a drink. As she is preparing your drink, the barista comments on what happened outside. "Did you see that woman who helped that man?" You say you had. The barista continues, "He has lived here for a long time. Anyway, do you want any milk or cream with your coffee?"
